edition: EPA Regional Screening Levels, November 2024: tap water 405290, resident soil 405274, industrial soil 405278, resident air 405282, summary 405270
rule: Each published cell is compared with the engine's unrounded value. It reproduces when the two differ by at most half a unit of the second significant figure of the printed value (the rule of the existing reproductions; the data holds at most two significant figures per column). Nothing is widened. A cell that does not reproduce is excepted under one of the classes below, or listed as unexplained.

classes.reason: The parameter sheet gives these volatile chemicals neither a soil organic carbon partition coefficient (Koc) nor a soil-water partition coefficient (Kd), so the engine's volatilization factor has no input and is not computed. The printed soil inhalation cell equals the level from the particulate emission factor alone, within half a unit of the second figure (the sweep checks this for every cell before it counts it here), so the tables applied no volatilization factor. The guide equation for Kd covers organics only and the guide text read does not say what the tables do without it, so these cells are excepted, not counted as reproduced.

The printed total adds the soil inhalation term of a chemical in the class above. The total built from the particulate-only inhalation level equals the printed cell within half a unit of the second figure (checked by the sweep for every cell before it counts it here). The volatilization factor is not computed for these chemicals, so the total is excepted, not counted as reproduced.

The summary prints key G (see user's guide) for lead and compounds. The database rows hold no slope factor, unit risk or reference value for them, so the engine has no level to compare with the printed one.
chemicals: Lead and Compounds (with other sources of lead present, see Guidance)

classes.reason: The summary prints key G (see user's guide) for refractory ceramic fibers, an entry in units of fibers. The database stores its reference concentration as 30000 and the engine reads it as a mass concentration in mg/m3, so the computed level is about a thousand times the printed one and in different units.

The tables print some toxicity values to three significant figures, so the value they computed with lies in the half-unit interval of the third figure, closed at its bottom and open at its top (a value at the top prints the next figure up). Two cases. (1) The inhalation unit risk of Aroclors 1242, 1248, 1254 and 1260 is printed 5.71E-4, so the value lies in [5.705E-4, 5.715E-4). The engine uses 5.71E-4 and computes the tap water total cancer level as 0.007852 ug/L, which rounds to 0.0079, while the tables print 0.0078; at 5.7118E-4 or more the total is 0.00785 or less and prints 0.0078, and the ingestion (0.039), inhalation (0.0098) and air (0.0049) cells of the same rows reproduce at either end. (2) The resident noncancer soil inhalation level of PCB 105 (printed 840 mg/kg): the tables print the TEF-applied reference concentration to three figures (1.33E-3), and the unrounded quotient 4E-8 / 3E-5 = 1.3333E-3 reproduces the printed 840 (the printed 1.33E-3 computes 833.3). The sweep excepts a non-reproducing cell only when the engine's levels at the two ends of the printed interval of the unit risk (cancer cells) or reference concentration (noncancer cells), which must need exactly three figures, meet the interval that prints as the cell. The unrounded value is not printed, so the cell is excepted, not counted as reproduced.
